sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Purchasing Power Parity & Decline**: When inflation rises, the real value of money drops, meaning a single unit of currency buys fewer goods and services.
• **Demand-Pull Inflation**: Occurs when aggregate demand for goods and services outpaces aggregate supply ('too much money chasing too few goods'). Driven by fiscal stimulus, low interest rates, or sudden surge in exports.
• **Cost-Push Inflation**: Occurs when overall prices increase due to rises in the cost of wages and raw materials ('supply shock' inflation). Driven by hike in crude oil prices, poor monsoons affecting food, or indirect tax hikes.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Measured primarily via Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Wholesale Price Index (WPI), with CPI acting as the nominal anchor for RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Mild rate of inflation, usually 0% to 3% annually.
Normal economic growth, healthy expansion of money supply.

Very high rate, double or triple digits (10%, 20%, 100%+ per year).
Severe monetary instability, loss of government credibility, major supply collapses.
Causes absolute distortion in capital markets; frequent comparison in macro MCQs.
Extremely rapid, runaway inflation (e.g., thousands or millions percent).
Total collapse of currency value, reckless unbacked printing of money by state.
Historical case studies (Zimbabwe, Weimar Germany) often tested via analytical statements.
Headline includes all commodities; Core excludes volatile food and energy items.
Excludes seasonal spikes to reveal underlying permanent trend of price movements.
RBI uses Headline CPI for inflation targeting, but analyzes Core inflation for monetary policy stance.

items.definition: A toxic economic combination of stagnant economic growth, high unemployment, and high inflation simultaneously. Defies traditional Keynesian trade-offs.
A fiscal or monetary policy designed to expand output and boost a sluggish economy back to normal levels after a period of economic downturn or disinflation.
A temporary slowing down of the rate of inflation. Note: Prices are still rising, but at a slower pace than before (not to be confused with deflation).

items.term: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) & Urjit Patel Committee
items.definition: Statutory body under RBI Act 1934 tasked with inflation targeting. Adopted CPI-Combined as the benchmark target of 4% (+/- 2%) recommended by the Urjit Patel Committee.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Rural vs Urban CPI Divergence**: Food inflation heavily impacts Rural CPI due to a higher weightage of food items, whereas Urban CPI is more sensitive to housing and services.
• **Regional Supply Bottlenecks**: Perishable agricultural goods face localized inflation spikes due to deficient cold-chain infrastructure across central and northern agricultural transport corridors.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Structural food price volatility, imported inflation via crude oil dependency, and climate change shocks affecting crop yields.
• **Policy Interventions**: Buffer stock management via FCI, dynamic export-import duty adjustments, PM-AASHA for price stabilization, and adoption of green energy transitions.

items.title: Mnemonic for Inflation Speeds
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'Can Gordon Hear Hyper Screams?'
• **Decoded Meaning**: **C**reeping -> **G**alloping -> **H**yper -> **S**tagflation (or Skewed).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Quickly recalls the severity gradient of price rise categories in matching-type questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Deflation = Negative inflation (prices fall). Disinflation = Positive but falling rate of inflation. Never confuse the two in UPSC statements.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'Disinflation means prices are falling.' This is incorrect; falling prices denote Deflation, while disinflation simply means the inflation rate is declining.

Mains Value Addition: In answers regarding supply-side management, mention how transitioning from price support policies to structural logistics improvements (PM GatiShakti, e-NAM) resolves structural inflation without hurting fiscal health.

keyTakeaways: Inflation diminishes purchasing power and is classified by its speed (Creeping, Galloping, Hyper) and origin (Demand-Pull, Cost-Push).
India utilizes CPI-Combined as the metric for inflation targeting, managed by the RBI's MPC at a target of 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2%.
Distinguishing between technical terms like disinflation, deflation, and stagflation is critical for cracking tricky UPSC Prelims exclusion statements.
